aiExplanation: This function finds the **longest contiguous subarray** where the product of all its elements equals the **LCM times the GCD** of those same elements. It uses two nested loops: the outer loop picks a starting index `i`, and the inner loop extends the subarray one element at a time to index `j`, keeping a running **product** (`p`), running **least common multiple** (`l`), and running **greatest common divisor** (`g`) so nothing has to be recomputed from scratch. Whenever `p === l * g` holds, the current length `j - i + 1` is compared against `max` and kept if it is larger. The helper `gcd` uses the classic **Euclidean algorithm** (repeatedly replacing the pair with `[b, a % b]` until `b` is zero), and `lcm` is derived from it with the formula `|a * b| / gcd(a, b)`, returning `0` if either input is zero. Both helpers also **memoize** their results in a shared `Map` keyed by a string like `'g:12:18'`, so repeated calls with the same arguments return instantly instead of recomputing. Note that the subarray check starts at `j = i + 1`, so single-element subarrays are never counted on their own, and the function finally returns `max`.

aiExplanation: This is a **brute-force** solution that looks for the longest contiguous subarray whose **product** equals the **LCM multiplied by the GCD** of its elements. The outer loop fixes a start index `i` and seeds three running values from `nums[i]`: the product `p`, the least common multiple `l`, and the greatest common divisor `g`. The inner loop then grows the subarray to each later index `j`, updating all three incrementally (`p *= nums[j]`, `l = lcm(l, nums[j])`, `g = gcd(g, nums[j])`) so each extension costs only a single step. If the condition `p === l * g` is satisfied, the subarray length `j - i + 1` is recorded in `max` when it beats the previous best. The `gcd` helper implements the **Euclidean algorithm** by repeatedly swapping in `[b, a % b]` until `b` reaches zero, and `lcm` is computed as `(a / gcd(a, b)) * b`, dividing first to keep intermediate values smaller and avoid overflow. Unlike a memoized variant, this version keeps the helpers lean with no caching, relying on the small input sizes to stay fast, and it returns `max` after all starting points have been tried.
